title: Grace removes both reatus and macula—else washing language fails
source_text: XV. Ex quibus omnibus certo & evidenter colligitur peccatum per Christi gratiam in fidelibus tolli, non tantum quoad reatum, seu obligationem ad poenam, sed etiam quoad maculam & pravitatem ipsam, quae animam inficit. Nam si Deus solummodo poenam peccatoribus debitam relaxaret, propter Christi meritum & satisfactionem, peccata vero quibus illam commeruerunt in animis eorum, sicut antea, haerere sineret; non obstaret ista poenae relaxatio, quominus in se peccato infecti, & servitute illius mancipati; vitiis aegri, imo in peccatis mortui, sicut prius manerent: adeoque dici non possent per Christi gratiam a peccatis abluti, mundati, & sanctificati; a servitute peccati liberati, a spiritualibus infirmitatibus sanati; ac denique a morte excitati, ut novam vitam cum Christo inchoent, non ambulantes amplius secundum carnem, sed secundum spiritum.
pass_a_gloss: From all which it is certainly and evidently gathered that sin is taken away in the faithful by Christ's grace, not only as to guilt, or obligation to penalty, but also as to the stain and the very depravity which infects the soul. For if God only relaxed the penalty due to sinners, on account of Christ's merit and satisfaction, yet allowed the sins by which they had deserved it to cling in their souls as before; that relaxation of penalty would not prevent them from remaining in themselves infected with sin and enslaved to its bondage; sick with vices, even dead in sins, as before: and so they could not be said by Christ's grace to be washed, cleansed, and sanctified from sins; freed from slavery of sin; healed from spiritual infirmities; and finally raised from death to begin a new life with Christ, walking no longer according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.
pass_b_english: Grace removes sin both as reatus (penalty-obligation) and as macula (soul-infecting foulness).
Mere penalty-relaxation without cleansing would leave us still enslaved, sick, and dead—unable to be called washed or Spirit-walkers.
